title: Browsing data lifecycle: server-side history with agent/user source, bookmarks, clear-site-data, permission-deny events, support export
summary: Derive a per-user visit log from Quarry session timelines, tagged source agent|user, retention-limited and disabled under ZDR, and show it in a history page with an agent filter and a short list of user-scoped bookmarks (or reuse Knowledge saved sources). Add clear-site-data on a profile by type and origin (cookies, storage, cache) with counts first. Make permission handling deny-by-default in the driver with a 'permission requested' event shown as an info chip. Add an opt-in, redacted export of a session's timeline and receipts to support tickets, never under ZDR.
whyItMatters: History and clear-data are table-stakes in both reference browsers and let users see and undo what the agent did in their profile; Verevon today only keeps a browser-local list of 10 entries. Category 1 deferred a consent-gated history query for agents to this item, so it also prepares a bounded read tool.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex in-app browser (history with Agent badge and source filter; clear-browsing-data dialog with counts; prompts keyed per page)
others: Aside (bookmarks, history panel, downloads bubble, privacy page)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: History and bookmarks: 2 of 3 sources, table-stakes. Clear data: 2 of 3, table-stakes. Permission prompts and diagnostics: 1 of 3 each, unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: History store deduplicated by day with favicons; each visit tagged agent|user; a settings page with search, delete-selected and a source filter; agent-facing history reads are gated by their own approval mode. Clear dialog maps selected data types and range to storage clears and shows counts first. Permissions: default deny for request and check handlers with a prompt store keyed per page. Diagnostics: opt-in tab diagnostics attachment and a bounded ring buffer of recent session events.

verevonToday.gap: No server-side history, no bookmarks, no agent/user tagging, no typed or ranged clearing of a profile's data, no permission events, and no browser-session diagnostics export.

approach: Ingestion Plane: visit log derived from the existing session timeline, tenant-scoped, TTL-bound, off under ZDR; clear-site-data endpoint by profile, type and origin (Storage.clearDataForOrigin, Network.clearBrowserCookies); explicit deny-all permission policy with events. Frontend Plane: history page in the browser settings hub (R-t2-08-07), clear-data options in the profile popover, bookmarks list. Gateway: opt-in redacted timeline export for support.
risks: Stored URLs are sensitive and must respect ZDR and retention; exports must be redacted and never include page data under ZDR.

verevon.exactGap: A durable, actor-bound per-run owner timeline already exists: StepReceipt plus BrowserTimelineEvent (Control events carry initiated_by human|agent|system), served by GET /v1/agent/runs/{id}/browser-session/timeline and refused with 409 for ZDR runs; saved profiles also have delete and a restore-probe that reports cookie, storage and IndexedDB counts, which the shell already renders. Missing: any cross-run per-user visit listing (StepReceiptStore lists per run only and quarry-edge has no list-runs route), per-visit agent|user tagging (receipt actor_id is the signed user for both drivers, timeline action items carry names and outcomes but no URL), bookmarks, clear-by-type/origin, any permission policy or event in quarry-browser, and a support export. The only history in the UI is the Nett search card's browser-local list capped at 10 entries (web-history.ts), unrelated to browser sessions.

verevon.constraints: ZDR: the owner timeline already returns 409 and receipts/timeline events are skipped for ZDR runs; a history view must keep that and never store URLs for ZDR runs (plan hard constraint, BROWSER_WORKSPACE_PLAN.md:25). Plane ownership: a visit log derived from receipts is Ingestion-owned (tenant and actor predicates), but bookmarks are user content, not browser evidence, and Quarry may persist durable knowledge only through Data Plane contracts, so they belong in a user-owned store outside Quarry (Data Plane saved sources, Application Plane or a gateway-side user store) with the Frontend only displaying them. Space authority: profile scope includes org_shared (any org member), so clear-data on an org-shared profile must be limited to its owner or an org admin and must not widen access. A stored-snapshot clear can race a live lease that re-saves the snapshot on release (the Kernel driver does, kernel.rs:194-200; not verified for the Chromium driver, INF), so it needs lease coordination.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into two deliverables. (A) clear-data plus permissions, S-M: implement clear-site-data as load, filter (cookie domain, storage and IndexedDB origin keys) and save on the stored SessionSnapshot through ProfileStore, with counts reused from restore_probe, and use CDP Storage.clearDataForOrigin only for a live session; add an explicit deny-all permission policy and a 'permission requested' timeline event in chromiumoxide. (B) visit history, M-L: add a tenant and actor scoped cross-run query on the receipt store (new Quarry route), project only host/path, time and initiator with a TTL, add initiator to receipts (or derive it from Control events) and keep it off under ZDR; put bookmarks in a user-owned store outside Quarry. Treat the redacted support export as a separate small gateway item that composes the existing timeline and receipts routes.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from M: five sub-features across three planes; history needs a cross-run receipt query, an initiator field and retention, and bookmarks need a store that does not exist. Clear-data plus permission deny alone is S-M.
verevon.verdictReason: Status partial and the gap is real, but the item understates the existing seam (a durable actor-bound owner timeline with initiator and ZDR handling already exists) and misplaces two parts: clear-data should mutate the stored profile snapshot rather than rely only on CDP calls, and bookmarks should not live in Quarry. Reword and split before scheduling.
